transcript.content: Hello, welcome in — I'm Dr. Smith. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

I’ve been having trouble keeping my mind on things at work. I’ll look at a loan worksheet or a client follow-up list and read the same line over and over. Then I put off making calls because even small decisions feel harder than they used to.
Over the past few weeks, have you been feeling down, sad, or hopeless most of the day, nearly every day?
Most days, yes. There’s this dull heaviness with me. Even at the community center or out in my garden, places I used to enjoy, I feel like I’m just going through the motions with a smile pasted on.
How long have you been feeling this way—this low mood and trouble concentrating—has it been going on for a couple of weeks, or longer?
It’s been longer than a couple of weeks. It really started after my close friend died, a little over two years ago.
Over these past two years, have you had periods—weeks or months—where your mood and concentration returned to normal, or has the low mood been essentially constant the whole time?
It’s been there pretty much the whole time since my friend died, a little over two years ago.
Have you noticed any physical changes over these two years, such as unexplained weight gain, feeling unusually cold, dry skin, or persistent fatigue?

Yes, the fatigue has been pretty constant. I wake up tired even after a full night’s sleep, and after just a couple of client calls or watering the tomatoes, I feel like I’ve already put in a whole day.
Have you noticed any unexplained weight gain or feeling unusually cold compared to before, over these past two years?
I haven’t really noticed either of those, no.

During these past two years of feeling low, has there been any specific period—say two weeks or more—when your mood and other symptoms became noticeably worse or more intense than this general baseline you've described?
I’m not really sure. It’s felt low for so long that I can’t point to a stretch where it clearly got worse than usual.
During this time, have you ever had thoughts of death or of hurting yourself?
I’m not sure what you mean exactly—do you mean like wishing I wouldn’t wake up, or actually doing something to hurt myself?
When you think about not waking up, is that more like a passive wish to escape how you're feeling, or have you had thoughts of actually wanting to end your life or hurt yourself?
I’m not sure. I’ve had days where I just don’t want to deal with anything, but I haven’t really sorted out what that means.
Over these past two years, have you noticed any changes in your appetite or eating patterns, such as eating much more or much less than usual?
I haven’t really noticed a clear change in my appetite or how I eat.
Over these past two years, have you noticed any changes in your sleep, such as difficulty falling or staying asleep, or sleeping much more than usual?
I haven’t noticed any real change in my sleep, no.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports a chronic, low-grade depressive mood persisting for over two years following a bereavement, with no clear symptom-free intervals of two months or more. Associated features include anhedonia, low energy/fatigue, and concentration difficulties, but appetite and sleep are unaffected, and there is no distinct period of acute worsening meeting full major depressive episode criteria. The chronicity (>2 years), continuous nature, and subthreshold severity relative to MDD, along with lack of a clear discrete episode, support persistent depressive disorder (dysthymia) rather than major depressive disorder or an adjustment disorder (which would not typically persist this long or this pervasively).
